utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milan Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, if I could, before counsel begins. I apologise. We would like to raise an objection, Your Honour. We refrained from objecting on several occasions yesterday for two primary reasons: One is, of course, we didn't believe that the conduct of the questioning would create issues with the Judges such as you might be concerned about with juries, and also because we did not know the length of the cross-examination, had it concluded yesterday, we would never have raised the issue, but because counsel has indicated that cross-examination may, in fact, even go beyond today, we do feel the need to raise an objection to the nature of the conduct of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Keegan, can you raise it quickly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that we are the Judges of facts and law, and it is for us to decide about the conduct of cross-examination. Can you put your point, as it were, in a sentence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I can, Your Honour. We believe that counsel is engaged in a pattern of misstatement of evidence and facts and it is resulting in unfair questions to the witness, and we believe the witness is entitled to professional and fair questioning, and we believe that has not been the case, and it was a pattern yesterday. As I said, we would not have objected had it ended yesterday, but since it's going to continue for we don't know how long, we believe it is an appropriate objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we will regard that as a shot across the bows. Do you follow? We won't rule on it at the moment, but they are minded to object if you misstate the evidence. But it is for us, of course, to determine whether there is misstatement. So far you haven't been stopped, Mr. Ostojic, although there has been considerable repetition. We recognise these are important issues for the Defence, therefore you have been granted some latitude. But if you could concentrate, as it were, on the particular issues, not repeat them. If there is any misstatement of the evidence, no doubt the Prosecution can point that out, but I am sure you will try and avoid it, and I think it would be in everybody's interests -- I don't want to put you under pressure -- but it would be in everybody's interests if we could complete this witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As I stated yesterday, we certainly will endeavour to complete Mr. Vulliamy today, but I must reply, if the Court permits, to the comments, because I certainly resent counsel using the word pattern which is a sensitive issue here, and trying to impugn that on my conduct here. If he could have, if he thought that it was so inappropriate, I think he should have raised it yesterday. I think it is inappropriate for him to use that kind of language when it is not my conduct that should be called in question on my questioning. Quite frankly from the answers elicited from this witness and the timing of the statements, it's not my conduct that should be called in question but the conduct of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, these are matters for us to rule on. Now, it would be better if we moved on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vulliamy. How are you?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Good morning, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we were discussing the meeting of August 5th, 1992, with you and various people in the municipal building. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Specifically, sir, I want to direct your attention to your testimony which was elicited through the Prosecutor's Office, and if I may be permitted to quote it so we have it in the proper context, it's at 10.09.32, and it states question by Mr. Keegan:

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: During this meeting, which is the meeting I represent to you as August 5th, 1992. Did you form an opinion who was in charge of the meeting, who was running the meeting? And you're giving the answer: We covered the control issue. It's something in the answer that I am seeking to cross-examine on, other than that issue. The answer at 10.09.42 seconds: "Well, thus far it seemed that the man doing most of the talking up until this point, if you like, the chairman of the meeting, or at least he was the one who was making the most pertinent remarks, and I found them interesting remarks because even before we had asked a question, we were talking about concentration camps and now he was defining what we were about to see is not a concentration camp but transit camps and talking about intelligence failure to identify the Nazi camps in the forties. I mean, I thought we were in the domain." And then you finally answer the last sentence: "Sorry. To answer your question, Mr. Kovacevic is the answer." Quote, unquote. So you answered a question that Mr. Kovacevic was in charge of the meeting. We covered that yesterday. But within this, sir, I was a little perplexed, and you state here and you seem to imply, and you can correct me if I'm wrong, that before the meeting even started, Dr. Kovacevic was in denial about either the transit centres or the concentration camps, generally that issue. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Those were his opening remarks, and I remember finding them interesting, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Now, I'd like, with the Court's permission, to direct our attention to Exhibit 48(B). For the record, that is the transcript of the tape that Mr. Keegan introduced. And if I may also ask that the Exhibit be tendered to the witness? And Mr. Vulliamy, if you can take an opportunity or a moment to look at Exhibit 48(B) and just let me know when you're complete so that I can proceed.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Sure. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, the first four pages of Exhibit 48(B) are what purports to be a translation of the excerpt of the tape that we viewed yesterday which was identified as Exhibit 48, does it not, or 48A, it may have been, does it not?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: It seems to be, yes, to the best of my recollection, these are the areas covered on the tape, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yesterday you were kind enough to tell us that before the tape started rolling on Dr. Kovacevic, before we actually saw him, there was an interval of five to ten minutes of that tape; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: As I said, I wasn't sure exactly how long, but we had come into the building, gone up the stairs, made some introductions. I can't recall how many minutes it was before the tape started rolling.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: The record will bear it out. Whatever you said, you said yesterday, and we're not going to debate it here today. If you look at the first sentence here, other than the caption, the foreign reporter in English states that the second promise was that we could see Omarska and Trnopolje. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Where's the first promise? We don't see it in these first four pages, right? Because it's cut off.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't recall what the first promise was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Right. And it was the first promise that we don't recall that's probably within that time period that I suggest you told us yesterday was five to ten minutes; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't know. I expect so. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Okay. That's fair. Now, if we look through the body of page 1, and we'll try to take this one step at a time, can you tell this Court how many times the tape was cut or there wasn't full usage of the tape, footage, other than the first five to ten minutes that I believe you testified to yesterday. Just looking at this first page, can you tell us how many times?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid I can't. I don't know about cuts in the tape --

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I suggest that you look on line 5.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: "We'd be happy to do that this afternoon."

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: What does it say after the word "this afternoon"?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: "Tape cut."

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Is that significant at all?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I honestly don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: It seems from reading this and I'm not a journalist or a TV reporter or producer, but when it says tape cut, what does it mean to you?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: It means the cameraman stopped filming.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Does it tell us here on this exhibit 48(B) how long he stopped filming?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: It doesn't appear to, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: You were at the meeting. How long did he stop filming; do you know?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: How long did the cameraman stop filming at this point?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: What I need to know, though, if you can recall at this point, did Colonel Arsic speak already? Did Dr. Stakic speak already before this first cut?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, I don't think so. Mr. Drljaca had certainly greeted us. I don't recall whether either Mr. Arsic or Mr. Stakic had spoken, but I am certain that the bulk of their contributions followed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I would think so too. Now, when's the next time that the tape was cut?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Well, according to this bit of paper I have in front of me, the next -- it says "Tape cut" at the end of the next line after the words "Television station, IT."

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: It's cut again, right? It's once again cut; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't know, but it says tape cut here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: You prefaced your answer by according to this document. Is there any other document that you know that exists that could help us flesh this out other than Prosecutor's Exhibit 48 B?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: As to what -- as to how the tape and when the tape was cut?

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't know. The tapes, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Was there any reason we should doubt that this was accurate, tape 48 B, that the tape was actually cut on these two specific instances?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I'm not ITN and I don't know when they were cutting their tapes or for how long. I wasn't following or directing the cameraman, so it's difficult for me to answer in a way that -- in a way that I can be confident of the accuracy. I've got a bit of paper and it tells me where the tape is cut but I don't know for how long or why or what. That's something that is not my province.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: When you say province, is it fair to say that it's not within your area of expertise?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: No. I would say that -- because I was there representing a newspaper and my job is to -- well, my job was to record the events in my book and in my memory, not to make a film. These people are making a film, and this thing tells me when the tape is cut. But I'm not in a position to give accurate information as to how long it was cut for or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Well, you were there and that's why I'm asking. You're presented as a witness. This exhibit was introduced. You discussed it. So I didn't mean to infer that you were the producer or the director or the man actually filming. What I need to know, since you testified just moments ago that after the first tape cut, it was at that point that Colonel Arsic point and that Dr. Stakic spoke, and yet there's another --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I will object. That is a misrepresentation of the witness's answer. He did not say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He said that he didn't recall, but he thought that the bulk of the answer came later. Yes. I wonder how much further we're going to get on this business about cutting the tape. Now, I recognise that there is no other witness that you can ask about it, but this witness didn't produce the tape, he wasn't the cameraman. He was there, so, of course, you can ask him about the interview and ask him about who was speaking and his recollection, but the actual technicalities are clearly not within his province.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour, but I do have some questions that I think it is my obligation to ask that are, I believe, are extremely important relating to the tape and the introduction of the tape and the manner that it was presented and introduced into evidence here, so if I may be permitted just a few more minutes to go into it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, if you look at the first four pages of this translated excerpt of the tape that we saw which started with Dr. Kovacevic speaking at the meeting, can you tell me how many times the tape was cut within that four-page segment? I counted six, sir. Can you count it for us? Just let me know what it is?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you how many times the tape was cut, but I can tell you how many times it says tape cut on these bits of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just for clarification, is there any reason we should doubt that, what's on this paper?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I haven't seen all the tapes. This is a translation of -- which, as I recall, corresponds with the tapes, although I'm not listening and reading at the same time, but what I'm going to do now, endeavouring to answer your question, is to count the number of times it says "Tape cut" and to see if we agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Actually, I count seven on the first four pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You just corrected me on it. It is seven, thank you. There's seven tape cuts on this four-page document; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: As I -- it says "Tape cut" seven times on the bit of paper in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to talk about the issue that we raised in your testimony the other day at 10.09.32 through 10.10.20 that we introduced before we got the exhibit so that we could discuss it somewhat. If you look, sir, the first time that Kovacevic raises the issue that you claim he started to deny before the meeting even began and that he started to deny the concentration camps almost immediately, can you tell me whether or not it appears on page 2, and if I may direct the witness, on the lower portion of page 2? It says Kovacevic, BCS, if I may just assist?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I think you're referring to the bit where it says interpreter, English article, saying they are concentration camps, not only Omarska and Trnopolje, but a list of about -- Kovacevic, BCS; "let me finish, first of all we know very well that." Is that the bit you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you could just continue, "first of all we know very well" --

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: "We know very well what concentration camps are. Interpreter English; first of all we know very well what are the concentration camps." Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Immediately preceding that section where Dr. Kovacevic mentions concentration camps, and I submit to you that your testimony with Mr. Keegan seemed to suggest, and I may be wrong, that Dr. Kovacevic, in light of your testimony today, started the meeting with concentration camps and that issue. Do you see that immediately before that, there is "Tape cut"? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So wouldn't it be fair that really, as you sit here now today, having all these people testify -- or the people gave their speeches, as you called them, at one point or introductory comments, we don't have that covered, but yet you recall, as you sit here six years later that Dr. Kovacevic started the meeting in denial?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I didn't use the term "in denial."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know you didn't.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: That's yours. What I have testified to and what my notes contain and what I testify to again is that during these first remarks or opening remarks, whatever we're calling them, the subject of concentration camps was discussed, both in terms of what is here, article saying they are concentration camps, that I think is articles about Omarska and Trnopolje, and Dr. Kovacevic's observations about how his people had, as I recall he puts it, "passed through concentration camps," and that how, I'm quoting from the bit of paper, "We know this better than the English people."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, on July 15th, 1998, a couple days ago, while Mr. Keegan was asking you at 10. -- five after ten and 23 seconds, you stated, and I quote, that the August 5th, 1992 meeting was, quote, "a very long meeting." Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, it lasted --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me be permitted to ask you a following question. How long was the meeting, because I don't think we actually established that?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I wouldn't want to put an exact time on it, but it was long enough for us to have a lengthy debate about whether we were going to Manjaca or not, for us to insist that we wanted to go to Omarska, to watch a video, to look at a map, and to go round the houses quite a bit as regards this question of Omarska, Manjaca, our safety and security, and the places that Dr. Karadzic had promised we could see. I don't know exactly how long. It started early to mid morning, and by the time we got to Omarska, it was lunch time, but I wouldn't want to put a time on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What is mid morning to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Mid morning is half past nine, ten o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What I really want to know, I don't want it exact because it's six years later, very difficult to recollect facts six years later and I'm sure we all understand that, give me your best estimate as an expert witness being a participant, if you will, at this meeting, how long was the meeting? Twenty minutes? Ten minutes? Thirty minutes?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Longer than any of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, give me an idea since apparently you know.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Well, I would say about -- about an hour and a half perhaps? You say my best estimate. I mean, that is an estimate. That is a guesstimate. I'm saying on oath that I don't know exactly how long that meeting lasted. It lasted long enough to have all of those round robin conversations during which we got impatient with what seemed to be filibustering, and it was long enough to get impatient.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How do you define filibuster?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: In this instance, I mean that Dr. Karadzic's promise was that we would see Omarska and this seemed to be running into some difficulties at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I really truly meant somewhat, and I apologise for saying it, but the definition for the word filibuster, the exchange. I'm just asking you what your best estimate was for the meeting. You said an hour and a half, and permit me to proceed. How long was the tape that we viewed on the meeting with Dr. Kovacevic that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, the witness hasn't estimated the length of the tape. That's a matter for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, to the best of your recollection, did the ITN cameraman and Penny Marshall and yourself, did you note whether or not the entire meeting was being filmed, the meeting of August 5th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Well, it's a subject -- it's a question better directed at them than me, but I would be surprised if they filmed the whole length of the meeting. I shouldn't think they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, were you actually in this meeting -- this was an important meeting for you as a journalist; correct, or foreign correspondent?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you were paying attention throughout the entire meeting; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Not all of it, I must admit. I was getting frustrated and quite bored by the round and round robin of whether we could or could not go to Manjaca and Omarska and our security, so, no, I have to admit, my attention drifted from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you have a recollection, on August 5th, 1992, when people were discussing at the municipal building issues with the foreign correspondents, that you lifted your chair and turned your back to the participants and folded your arms just like you're folding them now and completely ignored them for a period of time?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Do I recall doing that?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: No, but I might have done.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And, sir, isn't it true that you actually did that also during the showing of this videotape that you stated Dr. Kovacevic and others introduced to the newsmen?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: That I turned my back --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Turned your back to him, correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: No, I think I -- I've got notes which are quite similar to what's on the video taken as he was talking. I was writing down what he was saying some of the time. If I turned my back on him, then -- no, I don't think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we may, sir, direct your attention to your three-page note or notes of the August 5th, 1992 meeting? I believe everyone has that, Your Honour, based upon our conversation yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Are these the hand-written notes, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Exhibit 57; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Exhibit 57.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fifty-seven was it, Your Honour? Thank you. Your Honour, at this point I would like to allow us to introduce into the record that portion that was read, involving Exhibit No. 57, to us yesterday morning so that it be part of the record during the testimony of Mr. Vulliamy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, you can put that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vulliamy, a quick question: An hour and a half or so meeting, you have how many pages of notes from that meeting?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Only three.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why do you say "Only three." Do you expect more for an hour and a half meeting?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I saw no purpose in writing down the long round robin about where we should or shouldn't go, what our security was. I mean, we were repeating ourselves all over again, and I think I got down the gist of the fact that these people saw some uprising going on in their area, it was getting repetitive, and as I've said, I was getting impatient, wanted to get on, and we weren't getting on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You were becoming impatient because you were sent and you had this list that you wanted to try to uncover or see for yourself certain centres or camps, as you've called them; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I was getting impatient because allegations had been published in my paper and elsewhere about Omarska, also Trnopolje, and others; and as I've already testified, Dr. Karadzic invited, challenged, asked to come and see for ourselves, and that's what we had come to do. I wanted to get on and do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to Exhibit number 57, if you could look at that, please?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, the first page on the first line, you wrote, I believe, chief of police, and after that, what do you write?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Komandant.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is that an English word?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: No, I can only presume that's the word that was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ask what that meant?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you look, sir, at this three-page document from your notes of the meeting, approximately being an hour and a half, et cetera, it looks to as that Dr. Stakic, if I have it correctly, starts to speak at the second half of page 1; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And he proceeds to continue and you're taking notes down for Dr. Stakic through the entirety of page 2; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So far Dr. Stakic, a page and a half; right?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yup.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Stakic apparently continues to have notes written by you on page 3 of 3, of Exhibit 57?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I note in the first page, if we could jump back there, when the person that you were taking notes of, you would write his name on the actual line opposed to on the side -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- so you'd write his name as a title almost, and then beneath it you would start describing for us what it was that that person may or may not have said; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yup.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And similarly you did that for Dr. Stakic; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yup.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And let's flip because we know Dr. Stakic is the next page and a half. Three of three. Now, do you see Dr. Kovacevic's name on the right-hand side or the left-hand side, I apologise, of this document, in the centre of the page?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you see an arrow that follows from the line or from the name "Dr. Kovacevic" with an arrow down to the last five sentences of page 3 of Exhibit 57?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are the last five lines attributed to Dr. Kovacevic or Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: The last -- Dr. Kovacevic comes in "We are trying to stop," that's marked with a line, and he goes on down to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But you didn't at this point put Dr. Kovacevic on the line, you put his name on the side; would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, it's on the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, yesterday you were kind enough to clarify an issue for me, and I appreciate it, on the control, and we spent some time on it, I understand ad nauseam, or somewhat ad nauseam on that point, but then you added an interesting thing and you talked about gesture, and there was some mention of it and actually probably a great deal of attention put to a gesture that Dr. Kovacevic made during the August 5th, 1992 meeting. Remember that?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't remember a great deal of attention being drawn to it. There was a gesture, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption. Can you show me on Exhibit 57 where you make mention of the fact that Dr. Kovacevic made this gesture with his hand?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: No, I make no mention of it, but it was talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, you've interpreted this gesture to mean something; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you've shared with us what I think you believe that interpretation is; right?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Enlighten me again and tell me what you think it is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has given evidence about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. I'm just laying the foundation, Judge, so I could proceed on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, isn't it fair to say, in light of Exhibit 48B that you have in front of you, the transcript of the tape that we saw and the fact that the beginning portion of the tape is cut and the fact that there's two cuts before Dr. Kovacevic is actually permitted to speak. That it was at that point that Dr. Kovacevic merely said, and at that point Dr. Kovacevic was following the speech and the introductory comments of Mr. Simo Drljaca, Colonel Arsic, and Dr. Stakic, after those three individuals, as the testimony has been presented by Mr. Keegan and the evidence from your prior testimony that we've established, it was at that point that Dr. Kovacevic was speaking, and it was at that point, isn't it reasonable, Mr. Vulliamy, that Dr. Kovacevic merely lifted his hand and said, "Let me finish, Dr. Stakic"?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't know what the exact translation was and I wouldn't claim to ask. My recollection is that Mr. Arsic's main remarks -- he may have said --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may interrupt? Merely we want an answer to the question and I know he's trying to editorialise. I believe whichever question I ask, the Prosecution will be able, if the Court permits, to either rehabilitate him or allow him to expand. We are really trying to narrow it down. But when the witness does elaborate on his answer, it is a bit frustrating, and all I want to know is whether or not he remembers that. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think the witness must be entitled to answer a question, it's an important matter, in his own way to what his recollection was. Yes, Mr. Vulliamy?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: The answer is I don't know exactly what was said because I didn't understand the language, don't understand the language, but I remember the gesture.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why don't we look on page 2 of Exhibit 48(B) and maybe you can understand it in English?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: What is --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The gesture and how it was interpreted what he said during the meeting where you claimed the gesture meant something totally distorted versus what the interpreter said the gesture was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't understand that question at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: He said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Are you going to put to the witness that this gesture occurred at a particular point in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm directing his attention to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's go to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm directing his attention to page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The bottom portion where Dr. Kovacevic speaks the last time on this page, BCS, and it says, "Let me finish."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we can ask the witness that. Mr. Vulliamy, do you recollect if the gesture appeared at that stage of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not even sure what page we're on on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Page 2, one, two, three, four lines up.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I remember the gesture, I saw it on the film, and I'm reading this. I don't know whether it's exactly the same place. I would -- if we look at the film again and the words match what's written here, then I'm sure that's right. But I can't say absolutely for certain because I don't remember the exact words in the original language, nor would I understand them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just let me interrupt for a moment. I don't recollect this. We can see the gesture on the film, can we?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may represent to the Court. This is exactly where the gesture and his continuation on the comment, after the tape is cut or spliced, whatever the proper word is, and then he speaks of that, and then he continues to talk about the issues raised; "that we know very well what concentration camps are," and I represent that it was Prosecutor's exhibit, I believe it's their interpreter here, it's not ours, so that's why I bring it to the Court's attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I don't think we're going to get much further on that, but, of course, if you want to ask any other questions about the gesture, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: One other one possibly depending on his answer also.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true, that proper etiquette, when someone is speaking that, in fact, you should let them finish before you interrupt them and engage in conversation?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes. But if what you say is -- if this section at the bottom of page 2 of the transcript is the same as the bit that I remember and the same as the gesture that's on the film or I think is on the film, then it's a little more, shall we say, decisive than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if you can look on page 5 of Exhibit number 48(B) which is yet another interpretation, if you will, of various portions of the tape. I'm trying to go through this rather quickly, Your Honour. Are you on page 5?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, on that page, page 5, is an interpretation, if you will, of a tape, presumably the first tape, maybe another one, could be a third one, and on this one, they start first and they talk about the first thing -- do you see that? The word "first" on the first line?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: "First, if there's anything," yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you compare it to page 1 of that, page 1 as we've already, and you have been kind enough to share with us, starts with the second promise "et cetera"; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The beginning of the tape, on page 5, and the tape, the introduction, before Dr. Kovacevic begins to speak at the bottom of that page, two lines from the bottom, how many times was the tape cut according to Exhibit 48(B) page 5?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: How many cuts are there -- you're asking me how many cuts there are on page 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, but if you know, sir, just from being at the meeting and if you could share with us how many times it was cut, you can share that with us as well. That might even be better.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I was at the meeting, yes, but the cameraman doing these cuts was working for somebody else. I honestly cannot tell you how many times during that meeting the tape was cut.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I understand that, and I appreciate that. So tell me, based on this, Exhibit 48(B) page 5, what, in accordance with what the Prosecutor tendered to us, how many times does it reflect the tape was cut here, before Dr. Kovacevic spoke?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I would say on page 5 of this transcript, and I don't know which bit of film this is, I'm just counting the words "Tape cut" on the page, there are four cuts, as I count.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, if -- and I direct your attention to the centre portion of the page 5 where it says Kovacevic BCS, and he starts to talk about, "I'd like to know," and then apparently the tape was cut?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I can see that written down, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, what it was that Dr. Kovacevic wanted to know as you sit here?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I have no idea. I'm afraid I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The tape is brought back to the interpreter after being cut and then Dr. Kovacevic says: "There is no," and then something was unclear, and then the interpreter again and then the tape was cut again; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, I can see, it says "Tape cut," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if this section here that Dr. Kovacevic was speaking of was the issue that you raised in your testimony on July 15th in relation to the concentration camps that Dr. Kovacevic seemingly was denying before the meeting even started?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I'm afraid it's impossible for me to tell just looking at this bit of paper. I don't know, honestly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't either. And it's doubtful that you can tell from looking at this and comparing it to the tape, wouldn't you agree?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's doubtful that we can come up with a conclusion as to what happened in light of what Exhibit 48(B) tells us, if we compare it to the tape, as to when it is that Dr. Kovacevic, in your opinion, started the meeting out by saying there were no concentration camps, there were only detention camps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You know, Mr. Ostojic, I'm going to stop you. We've been through that point. The witness has given his recollection, and we have the document and also the tape, perhaps more importantly, and we'll have to make a judgement about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, page 9 of the Exhibit 48(B) -- are we there?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Page 9, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Now, this apparently is a transcript of the excerpt regarding the meeting with Kovacevic after the visit to Trnopolje; do you see that? It's right on top in bold, actually?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes. I ought to say that I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That was my question. Just for clarification. You weren't at that meeting at all; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: No, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Where did you go -- pardon me. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't have a date for this exactly, but as I've already told the Court, I went over to try and investigate camps containing Serbian prisoners over on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So it's fair to state, just so that I'm making sure I have it down, that the one time that you met Dr. Kovacevic in all of 1992 was what we have, and the notes that you have from that meeting definitively are these three pages from your notebooks; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No meeting afterwards, no meeting in '93,'94, '95?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me ask something, Mr. Keegan, I notice that this interview after the meeting at Trnopolje is attached to this exhibit but it has nothing to do with this witness at all. Are you calling some other evidence about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: We may, Your Honour, but we offered the exhibit and it was admitted. It was shown to the Defence, it was admitted. We believe it stands for itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: They may not have understood the point. But there we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I can reply to that point very briefly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll take notice of this at the moment--

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like to move along and proceed with an issue involving the camp of Trnopolje, okay?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in that -- during your visit at Trnopolje -- I kind of coined it as the barbed wire kind of issue, would that be fair? You stated for us that there was barbed wire there; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, there was barbed wire.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, what I'd like to know, and in your book on page 202, and I'll quote it. I apologise to the Court actually, I had the book and on my journey here while reading it I misplaced it on the seat, we do have accurate notes and we checked it yesterday and counsel who I believe is familiar with it, at the very least, and I can represent to the Court that these are actual quotes, so ... On page 202 of your book which involved the Bosnian issue, you state: "With his rib cage behind the barbed wire of Trnopolje, Fikret Alic has become the symbolic figure of the war on every magazine cover and television screen in the world." Do you remember saying that in your book?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, you also describe in your book his view of Trnopolje camps, or your view of the camps, I should say, and you write on page 104 that it's, quote: "Another startling calamitous sight, a camp" and then you mention a couple of words, "a camp surrounded by barbed wire fencing." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In your discussions with Mr. Keegan, and we saw the tape not only through your testimony but Mr. Sejmenovic's testimony several days ago, we saw Trnopolje and the camp with people walking, but I noted and I tried to read it as carefully as possible, in your testimony with Mr. Keegan did you or did you not tell us whether or not the barbed wire fencing surrounded the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't remember whether we talked about the actual fencing. The barbed wire was separating the prisoners from us when we first arrived at the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, those words are clear, yet in my opinion are unclear. They were separating you because you were on one side of the fence and they were on the other side; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yeah. We were on one side of the barbed wire fence and they were on the inside of the barbed wire fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that you were on the inside of the fence when you took that footage?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: No. They were the ones who were contained. We had stopped our vans and come from the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, isn't it true, and are you familiar with criticism that has been attributed to this barbed wire footage that, in fact, says that the unused video portion -- and if I may be permitted to say, we hope to connect this and I expect we most definitely will with our witnesses in our case in chief, but that the wire fencing around the fence -- strike that. That the barbed wire, that there was no barbed wire surrounding the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: The barbed wire did not go all the way around the compound, there was other forms of wire and a wall, but the barbed wire was between them and us when we arrived at the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why did you say in your book, sir -- I apologise. I try not to ...

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: You asked me if I was familiar with the criticism. Yes, I am. It's been going on a long time. It is the subject of litigation in my country, and I would be most grateful if I could perhaps give some background to the Court about this or we could proceed with questions at the Court's pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, let me see the point. The issue is whether there was barbed wire around the camp at all; is that what you're suggesting? That there was no barbed wire around the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: There was no barbed wire surrounding the camp as this man wrote in his book and there was only a section of the centre where there was a barbed wire. And what they did, in essence, according to the criticism, which we hope to connect, was that they came to an area where the wheelbarrows were kept and maintained and purposefully put the people that were within Trnopolje on the opposite side of the fence wherein they stood where the wheelbarrows were standing and taped them from a position that you could tell behind them was not the camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So we have the point that this barbed wire was inside the camp and that the photograph was in some way manufactured. That's the essence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Manufactured or distorted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Or whatever. No doubt the witness can deal with that briefly.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, I'll be as brief as I possibly can. This is a theory which was -- which I first heard about as written up by a man called Thomas Deichmann who was a Defence witness in the Tadic case, and who somehow got to view ITN material which was disclosed having been given to the Prosecution. The gist of the thing was that, as you've just said, we -- to quote you, "put people." We didn't put people anywhere. I'll continue with that later. This claim that somehow we were inside a compound and that these prisoners were outside a compound first appeared in Britain by Mr. Deichmann in a magazine called Living Marxism which is the journal of a party called the Revolutionary Communist Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you. We're not concerned with -- I'm going to stop you. We are not concerned with Mr. Deichmann. I think what would be most helpful, if you would just to tell us what happened when you arrived where the men were, and how the photographs came to be taken.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I would be delighted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would tell us that, please.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: We were going to Trnopolje from Omarska. We were arriving at the Trnopolje camp. I was in one bus, Penny Marshall's crew was in a mini van just ahead of us, we saw this extraordinary sight of this crowd of men behind a barbed wire fence. Penny's van pulled up. She got out, understandably, she's a television reporter, very quickly and made towards the fence. I followed. Our van obviously pulled up behind. I followed. The conversations that we had with the men, as I've described in my testimony, were through the barbed wire fence. They were in a compound which was enclosed, and there were guards guarding them in the enclosure. Suggestions to the contrary are the subject of what I said defamation proceedings in my country. That is how we came to find the men behind the barbed wire fence. The allegations incidentally have been retracted in the high court in my country by the press agency who repeated them, with an apology and no damages paid.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, in your book you state that it was surrounded by barbed wire and I move my fingers, in quotes, "surrounded by barbed wire," I want to know before we look at the tape is it your testimony that the camp was surrounded by barbed wire, sir?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I will testify now that the one fence through which we first encountered this group was barbed wire, some of it old, some of it brand new. The other fencing was chain-link wire of a kind that is used in prisons in the United States and patrolled by guards. As I recall, at the back there was a wall of a building. They were -- I mean, the conversation we had with them was through barbed wire.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We're familiar with that conversation and I think you shared that with us and thank you for that. When you say one fence, what does that mean? That only one section of Trnopolje had a barbed wire fence near it, or are you saying one fence, that it was complete and continuous, as you state in your book on page, as I said, 104 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've put that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I've put that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Sorry, could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When you say one fence, what do you mean by that? Was it a continuous fence?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: There was a continuous fence around three sides of the compound. The barbed wire was certainly all along one of the sides of that fence, and that was the fence through which I was talking to Mr. Alic and other people whose testimony I read out yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to flesh out, and I appreciate it. So if we take the centre, Trnopolje, if we take Trnopolje, you said from your recollection that there was a fence on three sides and on one side was the barbed wire fence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Can you repeat that? Sorry. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We're talking about Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you said that there was a fence generally on three sides; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: The compound was fenced in on three sides, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And on one of those three sides that it was fenced in, had this barbed wire where you had the initial first, purportedly, conversation with these --

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Where I had the conversations with these people, through the barbed wire fence, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's fair. Now, the other portions of the fence, what were they? They weren't barbed wire because I think you would have shared that with us, so I am curious to know. What kind of fence was it?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I will say now I am not sure whether the barbed wire went all the way around. There was other kinds of wire, certainly chain-link wire, and guards patrolling.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll talk about the guards at a later point. Just talking about the fence. The other side of Trnopolje, there was no fence?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: How do you mean the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, the fourth -- if you look at it, you said there were three sides, so I'm assuming then there's a fourth side; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes. This wasn't the whole Trnopolje camp, this was a compound within it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Oh, so this fence that you're talking about was actually within the actual large area of Trnopolje; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes. I talked yesterday and before about a school premises into which I went, and that is a different bit of the camp. I don't recall what the fencing or otherwise arrangements were there. The bit that we arrived at first was a compound, and that's, I think, the compound we're talking about, so when you say the fourth side of Trnopolje, that's not actually right. If you say the fourth side of that compound at Trnopolje, then I understand you, and I'm saying that that was a wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So we have -- just so I understand, and I'm not very clear on this and it really has been frustrating for me over the last several days to understand it -- we have Trnopolje, right? Okay, right?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: We have the complex of Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The complex. We'll use your words so I can understand. The complex of Trnopolje. Then within the complex of Trnopolje, we have what you call the compound, quote, unquote; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So within the complex is this compound.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: That's fair, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just trying to use your words and understand it. And it is within Trnopolje's complex that there's this barbed wire fence that surrounds a portion of a compound, correct, on three sides?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Barbed wire and chain-link wire fence surrounding three sides of a compound in which the prisoners were that we first beheld, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember as you sit here where this compound is within the complex?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Well, I don't know which is south and which is north, east, or west, if that's what you're asking, but if you're coming from Omarska, as we were, you get to it first and it's on the left, on a corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How large, if you recall, was the Trnopolje complex?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: How long large? Pretty large. A school, its premises. As I recall, another building, maybe two, and the field compound or whatever it was in which the prisoners were being held. How large is large? Yes. There was a lot of people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, I understand that and we've covered how many people were there. I don't know what pretty large means to you. Was it a square mile? Was it ten miles, the Trnopolje complex?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't want to measure it because I don't know, but it was certainly more a square mile than a square -- than ten square miles, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about the compound? How big was the compound that you're describing where there was the barbed wire fence on one side and chain-link or some type of fence on the other two sides, how big was that area within the complex, just so I can visualise it?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I'm really not trying to be difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, I --

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I'm trying my best to talk in terms of yards. If I said a medium-sized field, would that be helpful? I don't want to start measuring yards and feet because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: In relation to a football field?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you, Your Honour. Let's say two and a half football fields.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is that of any assistance to you, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. But just so I understand. Is the Trnopolje complex two and a half football fields or is the compound itself within that two and a half football fields?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: The compound in which the prisoners to whom we first spoke through the barbed wire fence was about, as I recall, and it is a guesstimate, two and a half football fields.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And using that same mode or rationale for measurement, football fields, and I do understand it and I appreciate it, can you tell us how big the complex was, now having told us that the compound was two and a half fields, just so we can have a perspective, if you will?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't really want to get into this measurement. But lets say --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It doesn't surprise me, sir.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Let's say several more football fields. Certainly bigger than the compound. I mean, there was more of it without the compound than within the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I figured that much out because of the way you describe the complex and the compound within, but I really need to know, sir, and I apologise for insisting on this question, but we need to know because you placed footage into this case trying to indicate that there was certain factual situations that arose within the Trnopolje compound, I need to know from you, the person who was there, how big that complex was in relation to the compound?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Well, I didn't place footage into the case, the Prosecution did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I stand corrected. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: The -- I'm trying to help here. The complex, the Trnopolje camp, was a complex of buildings, as I recall, the principal one of which was a school building. There was another building, if not two more buildings. There was more acreage or square footage beyond the fenced-in compound than there was within the fenced-in compound, that is to say, the fenced-in compound was the first bit that we got to, and behind it or further on into the complex, there was more space, more open ground, and buildings, principally this school building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I am going to stop this cross-examination now on this particular point. It's been taken as far as it can be. It may be that the Prosecution will be able to assist in due course with further evidence about this -- or the Defence, indeed, with further evidence about the complex. There is an exhibit -- I haven't referred to it -- Exhibit 45, but that shows the village as well as the complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would like to move on, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just to backtrack, one point that I missed regarding the meeting with Dr. Kovacevic on August 5th, 1992, and we hope after a timely break, we'll be given an opportunity to coordinate with the videographers and place a tape on this issue, if the Court permits, and others. On Exhibit 57, going back to it, and I apologise, you write on page 1 of that three-page exhibit the word T-shirt, and you put it in a square; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Sorry, which exhibit is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's your notes, I apologise?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From your August 5th, 1992, one and a half hour meeting. You're with me?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yeah. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you see the T-shirt there?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When was that written in?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: As we sat down, when I was writing down these names.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Whose T-shirt was it? Was it the guy next, the president of the commune, Milomir Stakic that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: No, it was an aide-memoire so that I wouldn't forget the T-shirt that Dr. Kovacevic was wearing, which was notable for the fact that it had U.S. marines written across it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that is why I wanted to actually ask you that, I didn't know if you noted that or not. In the videotape there was a footage, and I think you'll recall it, when the camera zooms into the side of Dr. Kovacevic's arm and zooms into what is a patch, if you will, on that T-shirt; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't remember that, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll share it with you later. But, in fact, the T-shirt that Dr. Kovacevic wore was a United States of America Marine T-shirt; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to clarify that. Thank you. Your Honour, we would like, if we will, to take perhaps an early break now so that we could coordinate the video footage or if the Court would like, we could do it, but I want to be a little more efficient and try to wrap things up as expeditiously as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What topic would you be going on to apart from the video? What else do you want to cross-examine the witness about?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have to cross-examine the witness in enormous detail, I must add, on his notes of February 1996 and his aide-memoirs, as he calls him, which were written, and the inconsistencies that I believe are exhaustive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That doesn't matter. So you want to cross-examine about that interview. Apart from the video and the video of the interview, is there anything more you want to ask about the camps. It is simply that it is rather early for us to have our break, and if we can fill in the time usefully, we should.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No. No, I'm not going to cover '92 any longer. I think I have covered it adequately, we hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So it's only the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. Right. The video is about 1992, as the Court knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. The registry has the video. Is there any reason we can't go on to it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not at all. I just wanted direction. I didn't want to interrupt the proceeding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The registrar can ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a couple questions that I could fill the time with, if the Court permits, but if the Court feels that I've covered this area more than sufficiently, I can wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we probably feel that you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I understand that we've coordinated it with the videographer, and if we may proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Play the part that you want to play, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Videographer, would you play the part? Just if we can pause here, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vulliamy, do you recognise this as being a portion of the tape that we saw yesterday? Do you recognise that portion?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Not yet, I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just do you recognise the house that's on the other side of that street there?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That building, I should say?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if it's a house or a building or part of a complex, that big complex you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: At the moment I don't know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could run the tape? Slowly, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At regular speed. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, now looking at this guy with the wheelbarrow, do the wheelbarrows, remind you of the wheelbarrows that were in front of the barbed wire within the compound of the complex of Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't remember any wheelbarrows.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you see the wheelbarrow there?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I can see a wheelbarrow in the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you have any independent recollection as you sit here, whether or not, during your interview with the people in Trnopolje, within that compound where the fence was, whether or not there were wheelbarrows on the side of the fence?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: There may or may not have been. I wasn't looking for wheelbarrows at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Please continue with the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any recollection of this being at least within the complex of Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I can't really tell from this, but if it is, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: See where these people are standing?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: It's very fuzzy, but I can see people standing there, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I agree with you that it's somewhat fuzzy. This building behind these people that are standing there, what is that building; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: It's hard to see, but it seems to be part of the Trnopolje complex, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall within that complex what specifically that building was?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I can't see from this picture, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can we maybe continue to play the tape, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Stop. Back up a little bit. May we back up a little? Let's stop. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is the camera trying to span over to the left, I believe, and it covered -- now the building that is seen on the right-hand corner a little more clearly. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like for us just to go backwards a little bit more. Continue: Pause, please. Is there a fence in front of these people here?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I can't see on this picture, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, when you were there, do you remember whether or not the fence was this close to that building back there?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't recall this particular bit -- it's difficult to see from the picture where it is, but I don't recall whether there was a fence or not there, but, I mean, as I recall, the fence went around the compound, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is this the area of the compound that you were discussing?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I think it's a corner of it, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can we proceed with the tape? The camera is spanning, and show me here during this picture -- pause, please -- our timing is a little off. Back up. And then if we can just slowly proceed forward again.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And Mr. Vulliamy, I'm asking you the question while the tape is running: Where within this picture do you see a fence?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Pause. Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I can't see the picture clear enough to identify a fence. There seems to be a fence running along sort of four-tenths of the way up but it's not very clear, but there seems to be a fence there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we can back up so we're clear on this point whether or not there's a fence on this side here. Stop. Pause, I mean. My apologies. Back on the tape, please. Now, this building, and if we can span it slowly again, is part of a school; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I think the whole complex was a school and its surrounding buildings, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the four-tenths of the way that you described. Sir, wasn't that just a fence that was an area to keep the children from going into different parts of the school complex, if you will? Stop.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I don't know. It was a fence within which the prisoners were being held.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, was that -- if you look -- continue forward, please? Pause. This purported fence that you see on this tape, that wasn't the barbed wire that you were discussing earlier that's on one side of the compound within the complex?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: That isn't the barbed wire fence, no, I think it's a chain-link fence, as I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Back on the tape, please. And we can continue to play the tape. Please continue to play it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This area is obviously the barbed wire fence that you were talking about, right?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, while the tape is simply playing, I would just make a point for the record, this is not the tape that was put in through this witness, this is not the ITN footage, this is the Serbian camera crew footage, so the first initial question was, is this the film we saw the other day? I presumed that meant through this witness, which is not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Pause, if you please. Pardon me Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's establish what this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may have asked that question, it certainly wasn't to mislead him. I thought that the registrar was giving us the tape that counsel placed in. This is a footage of a another -- I think of a another cameraman, if I'm not mistaken, which shows a view of Mr. Vulliamy here towards the end of this fence, and I think that that was given to us, though, if I may represent that, by counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, lets put it to the witness, if you wish. It's clearly the same scenes as we saw before.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, these are approximately the same scenes that we saw before; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, if that's the barbed wire fence, that's the fence through which we were talking to the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can we come back to the tape, please? Now, just let this portion or segment of the tape. Do you see where you are on that tape?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I think so, yes. Is that me holding the notebook? It's very fuzzy and the lights are right on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: But, yeah, that looks like me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we can -- if we can back the tape up just a few segments and then just come across it and then pause at this point again?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Now I can ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you see the post that is here in the left portion of the tape?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, I can see a post.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you see that post with the top wire up on top there, the first wire?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Does that wire extend on the left side of the post, if you can tell from this picture?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: I can't see it extend anywhere. I can see it going to the post.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It goes to the post. That's what I saw. I just don't know if my view of it is any different than yours or anyone else's. Doesn't it suggest, sir, this segment, that wire, the barbed wire that you were talking about, actually stops at this post, and you're actually talking to individuals at Trnopolje on the other side of the post or on the side of that post; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: At that point, that's fair. I interviewed several prisoners. The ones I interviewed through the barbed wire I've already told the Court about. Here I am interviewing some other prisoners. As you can see, to the left and behind Penny and I is open space with no crowd of people and within the fence is a crowd of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, do you see what's near your feet?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD VULLIAMY
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I have to say, I don't remember them, but they are wheelbarrows. I had other things to think about at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I understand that. That's why I direct your attention to it because you didn't recall it and you shared that with us.
